how.title: How validating works
how.stakedTitle: The node's key is the validator
how.stakedBody: The key that stakes is the key that validates. Your node signs blocks with its identity key in node-keys.json, so stake from that exact key (for example rougechain --node-keys <path> stake 10000), or import that key into your wallet before staking here. Staking from a different wallet does not make your node a validator.

stake.title: Stake XRGE
stake.body: Lock at least 10,000 XRGE from the validator key (10k standard · 100k operator · 1M genesis).

run.title: Run the node with --mine
run.body: Start a node whose node-keys.json is that staked key, with --mine, and keep it online with peers.

propose.title: Propose and vote
propose.body: The designated proposer for each height is chosen from the stake-weighted set; blocks are signed with ML-DSA-65.

reliable.title: Stay reliable
reliable.body: Missed turns freeze a proposer; slashing and jailing follow repeated misses or double-signing.

genesis.title: Become a Genesis Validator of the first post-quantum L1.
genesis.lead: RougeChain is live, quantum-resistant, and permissionless — but a network is only as decentralized as the people securing it. We're recruiting the founding cohort of independent validators. A call for operators, not speculators.
genesis.honestTitle: Read this first — the honest part
genesis.honestBody: Right now, validating RougeChain earns almost nothing: there's no token emission, the reward reserve is empty, and on a young chain fees are near zero. Don't join for yield. Join to be a founding operator of a chain built for the one thing every other chain is ignoring — the day quantum computers break today's cryptography. The economics come later, if the chain earns them. The role, recognition, and position are available now.
genesis.getsLead: No inflation was created to fund this — it runs on recognition, existing fee share, and treasury XRGE grants, not newly minted tokens.

recognition.title: Founding status, on-chain
recognition.body: A permanent Genesis Validator badge, your node named on the network map, and a listed spot on the public validator leaderboard.

weight.title: A real stake, not a cameo
weight.body: Consensus weight comes from self-staked XRGE — so genesis validators receive a treasury XRGE grant to stake as their own, and the team steps its own stake down over time. Your vote and fee share actually count.

grant.title: Cover your costs
grant.body: A monthly XRGE grant for the first 6 months to cover server + gas while fees are thin. A bridge to real fee volume, not a salary.

support.title: Direct onboarding help
support.body: Hands-on setup, a private operator channel, and first look at upgrades. You won't be debugging alone.

voice.title: A say in what's next
voice.body: Genesis validators get first input on the decisions that matter — including whether RougeChain adopts a sustainable staking emission.

mission.title: Secure something that matters
mission.body: You'll run consensus on the first production L1 that's already post-quantum. That's the pitch. If it doesn't move you, this isn't for you — and that's fine.

stake.v: Hold and stake at least 10,000 XRGE from your validator key — trivial to acquire; the barrier is commitment, not capital.

node.v: A reachable node (1 vCPU / 1 GB / 5 GB is enough) with a public URL, kept online.

uptime.v: Target ≥ 95%. Missing 50 blocks auto-slashes, so treat it like infrastructure.

keys.v: A dedicated validator key (never your treasury), backed up, and never run on two nodes at once — double-signing is slashable.

independence.v: You are not the founding team. The whole point is that you're someone else.

commitment.v: A 6-month run so the cohort is stable enough to mean something.

apply.body: Tell us who you are and where you'll run.

spin.body: Follow the <link>validator guide</link> — it generates your identity key (node-keys.json) on first run.

fund.body: stakes the exact key your node signs blocks with.

live.body: Run with --mine, then validator-status until every check reads ✓. We fund your stake grant, badge you, and you're in.

genesis.fyi: FYI — the "no yield yet" reality is by design, not neglect. A sustainable staking emission is on the table as a deliberate, holder-visible decision — and genesis validators help make that call.
genesis.ctaBody: Ten operators. Real independence. The founding validator set of the first live post-quantum L1. If that's you, step up.

node.title: Run a node
node.lead: Help power the network. Prerequisites, commands, and the live status of the nodes this page can reach.
node.scanningBody: Checking the network API and local ports 5100–5104.
node.noneBody: Start a node to see it here. Local nodes on ports 5100–5104 are detected automatically.

needs.computer: A computer or VPS (1 vCPU / 1 GB / 5 GB)
needs.tooling: Docker, or Rust to build from source

docker.title: Option A: Docker (fastest)
docker.body: No Rust needed — one command and you're running. Skip to step 3 once it's running.

rust.title: Option B, step 1: Install Rust
rust.body: If you don't have Rust yet, run this in your terminal. It takes about 2 minutes.

build.title: Step 2: Download and build
build.body: Clone the code from GitHub and build it. This takes a few minutes the first time.

start.title: Step 3: Start your node
start.body: Your node connects to the network, syncs the chain and starts running. --genesis and --chain-id are required to join mainnet — without them the node builds its own genesis and refuses to sync.

name.title: Optional: name your node
name.body: Show up with a name on the network map with --node-name.

node.validatorLead: Validators are nodes that propose blocks and vote. The node's identity key is the validator: it must hold at least 10,000 XRGE of stake.

find.title: Find your node key
find.body: On first run the node writes its identity key to node-keys.json in its data dir. That key signs every block your node proposes.

fund.title: Fund that key
fund.body: Send at least 10,000 XRGE (plus fees) to the node key's address. Bridge from Base or buy XRGE first if you need to.

stake.title: Stake from that key
stake.body: Run rougechain --node-keys <path> stake 10000, or import that key into a wallet and stake on the Validators page. Staking from any other wallet does not make your node a validator.

mine.title: Enable mining
mine.body: Restart the node with --mine and keep it online with peers. Check validator-status until every check passes.

node.testnetHint: These commands join mainnet. For testnet, use the testnet genesis and chain ID from the node README.

agents.title: AI agents on RougeChain
agents.lead: RougeChain ships a Model Context Protocol server. AI agents can query chain state, use DeFi, deploy contracts and manage wallets — all through a standard protocol.
agents.flowNote: Agents communicate via stdio over the MCP protocol. All on-chain operations keep post-quantum guarantees (ML-DSA-65 / ML-KEM-768).
agents.toolsLead: {{total}} tools across {{cats}} categories — {{read}} read-only, plus {{write}} that sign real transactions. Write tools activate when the server is configured with a wallet.
agents.installNote: Or use npx @rougechain/mcp-server directly — no global install needed.
agents.configTitle: Add it to your agent config
agents.writeNote: Add ROUGECHAIN_MNEMONIC to unlock the {{count}} signing tools. Every transaction is signed locally with ML-DSA-65 — your seed phrase never leaves the server. Use a dedicated low-balance agent wallet; generate one with the generate_wallet tool.

regen.sub: A regeneration program & treasury on RougeChain
regen.title: Fund the future where you live.
regen.lead: RougeChain Regenerate connects digital infrastructure with real-world regeneration — funding transparent, measurable projects that improve the communities and ecosystems around us.
regen.statement: Technology should improve the territory it touches.
regen.statementBody: Global problems are real, but change becomes tangible at the local level. RougeChain Regenerate begins with communities, ecosystems, and infrastructure we can actually see, measure, and improve.
regen.solarpunk: A solarpunk stance: technology, architecture, art and community building a future worth living in — not just one that survives.

infrastructure.title: Regenerative Infrastructure
infrastructure.blurb: Solar, water capture, gardens, composting, community energy.

technology.title: Open Technology
technology.blurb: Environmental sensors, mapping tools, public-infrastructure software, open-source climate tech.

art.title: Art + Community
art.blurb: Public installations, education, workshops, community spaces and solarpunk projects.

tulum-mangrove-01.name: Mangrove Corridor Restoration
tulum-mangrove-01.description: Replant and monitor degraded mangrove sections that buffer the coastline, filter water, and store carbon — with community stewards and open survey data.

tulum-cenote-water-02.name: Cenote Water-Quality Sensor Network
tulum-cenote-water-02.description: Low-cost, open-source sensors monitoring the cenote and aquifer system, publishing readings openly so the community can see water health over time.

tulum-community-solar-03.name: Community Solar + Water Capture
tulum-community-solar-03.description: Shared rooftop solar and rainwater capture for a community space — resilient local infrastructure that keeps running when the grid doesn't.

regen.territoryBody: Regeneration should begin somewhere real. RougeChain Regenerate will begin by exploring projects in Tulum, where technology, ecology, culture and rapid development intersect.
